extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys/agents, patent applicants, and USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reading and interpreting the Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP) front-matter notations, revision indicators, and hyperlink/format conventions used throughout the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision Date Indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section within an MPEP Chapter includes a revision date indicator, e.g., [R-01.2024]. The numbers within the bracket indicate the date the revision cycle for that section was completed (January 2024 in the example). Note that the publication date of the Manual as indicated on the title page and on the bottom of the PDF renderings may be later than the date the revision cycle was completed because of the time required for clearance processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bracketed [R-MM.YYYY] indicator to determine when the revision cycle for that specific section was completed rather than relying solely on the overall publication date; expect the publication date to sometimes be later due to clearance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Pre-AIA" designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Pre-AIA." Where the phrase "pre-AIA" is associated with a law or rule, it means that version which was in force before the date of the change necessitated by the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act (AIA), Public Law 112-29, 125 Stat. 284.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a section or statutory discussion is labeled "pre-AIA," treat it as applying to the pre-AIA statutory/regulatory regime; do not conflate pre-AIA rules with post-AIA rules unless the text explicitly addresses applicability to both.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Pre-PLT" / "pre-PLT (AIA)" designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Pre-PLT" or pre-PLT (AIA). Where the phrase "pre-PLT" or "pre-PLT (AIA)" is associated with a law or rule, it means that version which was in force before the date of the change necessitated by the Patent Law Treaties Implementation Act of 2012, Title II (Patent Law Treaty Implementation (PLT)), Public Law 112-211, 126 Stat. 1527 (Dec. 18, 2012). Note that the "pre-PLT (AIA)" designation is used when there is also a "pre-AIA" version of the law or rule that still has applicability in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret "pre-PLT" and "pre-PLT (AIA)" labels as indicating the applicability of pre-PLT procedural rules; where both "pre-PLT (AIA)" and "pre-AIA" designations appear, pay attention to which pre-change regime applies in the specific limited circumstances described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five Asterisks notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Five Asterisks. The use of five asterisks in the body of the laws, rules, treaties, and administrative instructions indicates a portion of the law, rule, treaty, or administrative instruction which was not reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When five asterisks appear, recognize that material has been omitted from the reproduced text; do not assume the reproduced snippet is complete or sufficient for legal citation without consulting the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlink rendering and copying convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Most hyperlinks from the Manual to internal and external websites are active. For particularly long website addresses (URLs), an extra space has been added to the rendered text for readability (especially in the PDF rendering). Clicking on a hyperlink will direct the user to the referenced website because the reference link data in the source document includes the URL without the extra space; however, copying text that includes the extra space and thereafter pasting it in a browser will result in an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click links directly when possible. If copying a displayed URL from the MPEP/PDF, remove any spurious space characters inserted for line-wrapping before pasting into a browser. Use the USPTO MPEP search engine (https://mpep.uspto.gov/RDMS) for reliable access to sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and archival access
rubrics_metrics.description: The paperbound format of the Manual was discontinued by the Government Publishing Office effective December 13, 2012. The Manual is available electronically in html and PDF renderings on the USPTO website at www.uspto.gov/web/offices/pac/mpep/. The Office also provides a search engine for searching the full text of the Manual at https://mpep.uspto.gov/RDMS. Previous editions and revisions of the Manual are available from the MPEP Archives page on the USPTO website at www.uspto.gov/web/offices/pac/mpep/old/index.htm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the electronic html/PDF versions and the RDMS search engine for authoritative and up-to-date MPEP text; use the MPEP Archives for historical versions and prior editions.
